Don't let volume commands starve the playback clock

Dragging the volume bar queues a "volume" command on every frame, and the
player loop's command branch skips the playback branch, so track() never
ran and pctl.playing_time stopped advancing while the bar was held. The
seek bar froze, and since track() clamps a catch-up to 2s and only resyncs
to the real position when it is out by less than 5s, the lost time was
never made up — the position stayed wrong for the rest of the track.

Handle volume ahead of the command branch, the same way run_vis() already
is, so playback still gets its turn on those iterations.

set_volume() made this worse: with a command already pending it spawned a
thread to re-send the volume a second and two seconds later, one per frame
of the drag, so the flood outlived the drag by seconds. A pending "volume"
command reads player_volume when the player runs it, so it already carries
the newest value and there is nothing to defer.
